question: Following the Supreme Court of India's 2018 judgment in Common Cause v. Union of India, passive euthanasia and the withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment are legally permissible in India under specific safeguards, including a valid advance directive.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The 2018 Supreme Court judgment (Common Cause v. Union of India) legalised passive euthanasia and upheld advance directives (living wills) in India. The Court held that the right to die with dignity is part of Article 21. Active euthanasia remains illegal.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The Supreme Court in Common Cause v. Union of India (2018) ruled that the right to die with dignity is a fundamental right under Article 21. Passive euthanasia (withdrawal or withholding of life support) with an advance directive (living will) is permitted under defined procedural safeguards. Active euthanasia remains illegal.
